title: Semi-automated micro-computed tomography lung segmentation and analysis in mouse models
author: Luisi, Lin, et al.

steps.title: Prepare mice and administer treatment
steps.instruction: Anesthetize mice and deliver 20 µL of saline, poly‑inosinic‑poly‑cytidylic acid (Poly‑IC), or bleomycin intratracheally (or intranasally) as described in the experimental design.

steps.title: Calibrate micro‑CT scanner
steps.instruction: Using the Siemens Inveon Micro‑CT system, calibrate radiodensity with air and water reference phantoms according to the manufacturer’s instructions before any animal scans.

steps.title: Acquire whole‑body CT images
steps.instruction: Scan each mouse with the following acquisition settings: 1000 ms (1 s) per projection, 70 kV X‑ray source voltage, 500 µA source current, 107 µm isotropic resolution, 360° rotation, 520 projections. The resulting field‑of‑view is 54.85 × 54.85 × 82.27 mm, reconstructed to 512 × 512 × 768 voxels.

steps.title: Export raw image files
steps.instruction: Save the reconstructed volume as a .HDR file (or as standard DICOM) for downstream analysis; note that each dataset is >1 GB in size.

steps.title: Install ImageJ and Bio‑Formats
steps.instruction: Download FIJI/ImageJ version 1.52h and ensure the Bio‑Formats importer plugin is installed to handle .HDR and DICOM files.

steps.title: Import CT data into ImageJ
steps.instruction: Open the .HDR (or DICOM) file with the Bio‑Formats importer, importing the stack as a 16‑bit float image. No additional pre‑processing is required.

steps.title: Run semi‑automated segmentation macro
steps.instruction: Download the ImageJ macro from the supplement or https://github.com/UTMB‑Luisi/SemiAutomated_Lung_CT and execute it. The macro automatically creates a connected‑components mask and segments the lung using the HU bins: –1000 to –700, –700 to –600, and –600 to –500 (additional bins –500 to –400, –400 to –300, –300 to –200, –200 to 0 may be defined as needed).

steps.title: Validate segmentation mask
steps.instruction: Visually inspect the automatically generated mask for each slice; accept the mask if lung boundaries are correctly identified, otherwise adjust parameters in the macro and re‑run.

steps.title: Calculate radiodensity and volume
steps.instruction: The macro computes voxel counts per HU bin, converts them to tissue volume (mm³) using the known voxel size (107 µm isotropic), and outputs a table of total lung volume and volume per HU bin.

steps.title: Save results and log processing time
steps.instruction: Export the volume table and mask images to disk. Record that each connected‑component volume typically processes in <30 min and the full analysis requires <5 min of user interaction.
